Read camera-trap data in Camtrap DP format

Source: R/camData.R
camData.Rd

Create a camReport object from a Camtrap DP dataset.

Usage

camData(data, habitat, study_area, update, ...)

Arguments

data

A character string giving the path to a Camtrap DP dataset, provided as a ZIP file or an extracted dataset directory.

habitat

An optional data frame containing habitat information for camera locations. The default is NULL.

study_area

An optional study-area boundary provided as a spatial file path, a SpatVector, or an sf object. The default is NULL.

update

A logical value (default FALSE) specifying whether to recreate a previously saved camReport object.

...

Additional arguments. These are currently reserved for future use.

Value

A camReport object.

Details

The function reads the input Camtrap DP dataset and creates a camReport object. The resulting object contains processed camera-trap data, metadata, summaries, report text, report modules, and data-status information used to generate automated reports.

If habitat information is provided, it is linked to camera locations and used in habitat-related summaries. If a study-area boundary is provided, it is stored with the object and used in spatial summaries where relevant.

The camReport object is saved within an extracted dataset directory as __camReport_Object.rds. A later call using that directory reuses the saved object unless update = TRUE, in which case the object is recreated.

data currently accepts a file-system path, not an in-memory data frame or list. A dataset directory contains datapackage.json, deployments.csv, media.csv, and observations.csv. The following identifiers and columns explain the main relationships; this is not a complete Camtrap DP schema:

FileContents and important links
datapackage.jsonProject metadata and a taxonomic list with species names, taxon identifiers, ranks, families, orders, and optional vernacular names.
deployments.csvOne camera deployment per deploymentID, with locationID, locationName, longitude, latitude, deploymentStart, and deploymentEnd.
media.csvImages or videos identified by mediaID, linked to deploymentID, with timestamp and optional capture-method and file metadata.
observations.csvSpecies or other classifications linked to deploymentID, mediaID and/or eventID, with scientificName, observation level, event times, counts, and optional individual measurements.

A deployment is a period during which a camera is installed at a location. An observation records a classification at media or event level. An event groups related media; camtrapReport uses sequenceID internally for this event grouping and derives a sequences table from media timestamps. These internal sequences are not an additional input CSV file. See the Camtrap DP specification for definitions and the example-data provenance for a concrete dataset.

Import and status() provide package-specific data checks, not formal validation against the complete Camtrap DP schema. Check schema compliance upstream. After correcting source CSV or JSON files, call camData() again with update = TRUE and the optional inputs, then regenerate status(). Merely rerunning status() on the old object does not reread changed files.

Files and cache reuse

camData() writes __camReport_Object.rds beside the extracted data and, when a study area is supplied, writes study_area.map. A ZIP input is extracted before reading. Use a writable copy of the input dataset, as in the examples, rather than an installed package directory. A cached object is reused when update = FALSE; changes to source files or optional inputs are not detected automatically. Use update = TRUE to rebuild it. Only load datasets and saved R objects from sources you trust.

Optional taxonomy enrichment

In the current implementation, installing taxize enables GBIF taxonomy lookups during import. Species names are sent to GBIF to supplement class and order information. This can require an internet connection and affect import time and reproducibility; there is currently no per-call opt-out or request-timeout argument. Preserve the processed object and package versions used in an analysis, and consider this network behaviour before processing confidential species lists. Without taxize, this lookup is not performed.

Study areas that change over time

study_area accepts one boundary per object. Multiple Shiny uploads are the component files of a shapefile (.shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj, etc.), not a set of year-specific boundaries. For different survey footprints, prepare separate year-specific datasets and objects with the corresponding boundary, or supply a custom module with an explicit year-to-boundary mapping.

See also

report(), status(), info(), gui()

Examples

# \donttest{
source_dataset <- system.file(
  "external",
  "dataset",
  package = "camtrapReport"
)
example_dataset <- tempfile("camtrapReport-example-")
dir.create(example_dataset)
invisible(file.copy(
  list.files(source_dataset, full.names = TRUE),
  example_dataset,
  recursive = TRUE
))

cm <- camData(example_dataset)

cm

unlink(example_dataset, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
# }
